description.narrative: In June 2023, the Government of Eswatini in consultation with the social partners validated and adopted a gender responsive diagnostic study that examined the incidence, forms, and drivers of diverse work arrangements with a particular focus on home-based workers. The diagnostic also examined decent work deficits confronting home-based workers in Eswatini. The diagnostic study entailed a gendered analysis of the situation of home-based workers, with particular focus on the policy and legislative environment or lack of, with a set of recommendations for consideration by the national partners to improve the welfare, livelihoods, and opportunities for home-based workers in Eswatini. The diagnostic found that home-based workers in Eswatini are overwhelmingly made up of women and overwhelmingly unregistered. It also found that registration is the crucial issue facing home-based workers, according to the workers themselves. While many home-based workers fear the tax burden that could come from registration, all recognize that there are significant advantages to be gained as well. Some of the findings of the diagnostic study fed into the review of the Small, Micro, Medium Enterprises Policy. From April - May 2022, the ILO carried out a series of discussions and sensitized the Government on the concept of home-based workers as a category of workers often ignored or unprovided for and in need of specific policies on the basis of which the ILO and the government decided to undertake a diagnostic study on home-based workers. Since the quantitative analysis of home-based work can be undertaken using the Labour Force Survey, the study emphasized the qualitative aspects and assumed the form of focus groups with home-based workers as well as interviews with policy-makers. In addition to the focus groups of home-based workers, key actors, including social partners, were interviewed. From April 2022 to May 2023, the ILO provided both technical and financial support in the planning and implementation of the gender-responsive diagnostic assessment and throughout the process. In June 2023, the ILO collaborated with the Ministry of Commerce, and the Ministry of Labour and Social Security to host and facilitate a tripartite workshop convened by the government for the dissemination and validation of the findings of the diagnostic study.

description.narrative: The Government of Eswatini and the Social Partners developed a National Labour Migration Policy (NLMP) and its accompanying Action Plan, that were adopted by the Labour Advisory Board in October 2022. In August 2023, Cabinet adopted the National Labour Migration Policy and its accompanying Action Plan. The Labour Migration Policy provides a governance framework for the Kingdom of Eswatini to effectively manage labour migration so that it protects all workers, develops the country’s economy, strengthens, and transfers skills, integrates returnees, and benefits the Kingdom and its subjects. Even prior to the Cabinet adoption of the NLMP, Government and the Social Partners mandated an already existing tripartite Technical Working Group on Labour Migration in April 2022 to oversee the implementation of five concrete activities in the Labour Migration Policy. These activities include the development of an Action Plan to operationalize the Southern Africa Development Community (SADC) Guidelines for the Portability of Social Security Benefits; integrating labour migration indicators in the last Labour Force Survey using guidelines of the latest statistical standards; strengthening national capacity for the analysis and dissemination of labour migration data from the Labour Force Survey; and support to the establishment of bilateral labour migration agreements to facilitate the portability of accrued social security benefits. With the support of the European Union, and in partnership with the International Organization on Migration (IOM), the ILO facilitated a tripartite dialogue on Labour Migration Governance in April 2022. The tripartite dialogue provided a platform for engagement by the partners on an existing draft NLMP and Action Plan and to make recommendations for strengthening the two documents. The country level dialogue also facilitated the identification of activities that would be supported for implementation by the Southern Africa Migration Management (SAMM) project. In July 2022 the ILO supported a meeting of the tripartite Technical Working Group on Labour Migration to review a revised draft NLMP and its Action Plan which led to further amendments to the text of both documents and strengthening of gender dimensions in the policy. Subsequent to the meeting of the Technical Working Group on Labour Migration, and still in July 2022, the ILO in partnership with IOM supported the Ministry of Labour and Social Security in presenting both draft policy documents to the Labour Advisory Board for its adoption.
